caption:
New ABN? 5 things nobody tells you in year one.

1. Nobody withholds your tax. An employer takes tax out of every pay. As a sole trader the whole bill arrives after you lodge, so the money has to be set aside along the way.

2. You can't pay yourself a wage. The ATO treats a sole trader's "wage" as a distribution of profit. You're taxed on profit (income minus expenses) whether you take it out or not.

3. GST starts at $75,000 of turnover, not profit. You have 21 days to register once you reach it.

4. Nobody pays your super. The 12% super guarantee is for employees. Sole traders make their own contributions (and can usually claim a deduction).

5. Year 2 brings PAYG instalments. Once your first return shows enough business income and tax, the ATO starts collecting the next year's tax as you go.

Which one caught you out?

#abn #soletrader #smallbusinessaustralia #firstyearinbusiness #australiantax
figures_checked: Sole traders and partners can't pay themselves a salary or wage: any nominal payment is a distribution of profit; a sole trader can usually claim a deduction for their own super contributions (ATO Deductions for salaries, wages and super contributions, checked 15 Nov 2026)
GST: register within 21 days of GST turnover reaching $75,000; ride-sourcing and taxi drivers must register regardless of turnover (ATO Registering for GST, checked 11 Nov 2026)

Payday Super from 1 July 2026: super guarantee paid for each payday, contributions to reach the fund within 7 business days of payday, rate 12%; super guarantee charge assessed by the ATO on qualifying earnings with daily compounding interest and an administrative uplift (ATO About Payday Super, checked 15 Nov 2026)

PAYG instalments entry for individuals incl. sole traders: instalment income of $4,000 or more on the latest return, tax payable of $1,000 or more on the latest assessment, and estimated (notional) tax of $500 or more; ATO notifies via myGov, online services or letter (ATO Starting PAYG instalments, checked 15 Nov 2026)
